question: A particular cell present in the excretory system of flatworms, which helps them removing waste materials is the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**flame cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Flame cells** are specialized excretory cells found in flatworms, such as Planaria, belonging to the phylum Platyhelminthes.
 
• These cells play a crucial role in the removal of nitrogenous waste products and maintaining osmotic balance in flatworms.
 
• Flame cells are part of the **protonephridial system**, which functions as the excretory system in these organisms.
 
• The name "flame cell" is derived from the flickering movement of cilia present inside the cell, resembling a flame.
 
• The cilia in flame cells drive the waste materials and excess water out of the body through excretory pores.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protonephridial System:**

 
 
• This system consists of a network of tubules and flame cells that facilitate excretion and osmoregulation in flatworms.
 
• It is considered a primitive excretory structure compared to advanced systems in higher organisms.
 
 
 
• **Flatworms (Platyhelminthes):**
 
 
• Flatworms are bilaterally symmetrical, dorsoventrally flattened, and lack a circulatory system.
 
• They rely on diffusion for nutrient and gas exchange, making their excretory system essential for waste removal.
 
 
 
• **Cnidoblast Cells:**
 
 
• These are specialized cells found in cnidarians (e.g., jellyfish) and are used for defense and prey capture, not excretion.
 
 
 
• **Osmoregulation in Flatworms:**
 
 
• Flame cells are pivotal in regulating the water content of the organism, ensuring it maintains homeostasis in aquatic environments.
